c.tagline: Lombok's laid-back provincial capital and gateway to the Gili Islands and Mount Rinjani.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird taxis are metered and reliable; app-based ride-hailing (Gojek/Grab) operates but can face pickup restrictions near the airport and traditional taxi stands due to long-standing local driver protections.

emergency.note: 112 is a nationwide emergency number that can route to police, fire, or medical services, though an English-speaking operator is not guaranteed.

avoid.reason: Bag-snatching from passing motorbikes occurs; keep phones and bags on the side away from traffic.

hood_desc: The historic port district with fading Dutch and Chinese colonial shopfronts, art galleries, and a lively Sunday street-art market along the coast; suits travelers wanting character and sunset views over the Lombok Strait.
The administrative and commercial heart of the city with government offices, malls, and the main square; convenient as a base with easy onward transport to the Gilis or Rinjani.
Lombok's busiest trading hub, home to the 18th-century Hindu-Balinese Pura Meru temple and the sprawling Cakranegara Market; good for street food and browsing local goods.
A craft neighborhood known for pearl and silver jewelry workshops where visitors can watch artisans at work and buy directly from makers; appeals to shoppers wanting authentic souvenirs.
A quieter, more residential area near the former Selaparang airport site; suits longer-stay visitors wanting a calmer, local-feeling base away from the busiest streets.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Angkot minivans and local buses generally run from about 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM; there is little to no public transit after dark.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the driver; angkot rides are flat-rate and inexpensive (roughly Rp 5,000-10,000), with no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.note: Mataram has no formal rapid transit; getting around relies on angkot minivans, motorbike taxis (ojek), Gojek/Grab, and rental scooters, which are also the most practical way to reach the Gilis ferry ports or Rinjani trailheads.

bus: Intercity buses toward Kayangan Port for Sumbawa connections
ferry: Bangsal/Teluk Nara harbor (boats to the Gili Islands)

transit.m: DAMRI airport shuttle bus to Mataram (~45 min)

tip.r: Tipping isn't traditionally expected; rounding up or leaving a small amount (Rp 10,000-20,000) for good service at restaurants and for drivers/guides is appreciated.

food.name: Ayam taliwang
food.desc: Young free-range chicken split flat, grilled over coals and coated in a chilli, shrimp paste, garlic and palm-sugar sauce. Lombok's defining dish.

places.name: Rumah Makan Taliwang Irama
places.note: Well-known Mataram taliwang house; order it with plecing and beberuk terong.

places.name: Lesehan Taliwang Nada
places.note: Floor-seating warung on Jl. Ahmad Yani doing taliwang and sate rembiga.

places.name: Warungs of Kampung Karang Taliwang
places.note: The neighbourhood the dish is named after, still full of grill houses.

food.name: Plecing kangkung
food.desc: Water spinach blanched and topped with a raw sambal of chilli, tomato, shrimp paste and lime, scattered with fried peanuts and bean sprouts.

places.name: Rumah Makan Taliwang Irama
places.note: Standard side with the grilled chicken; sharp, fiery sambal.

places.name: Taliwang Khas Pak Udin

food.name: Sate rembiga
food.desc: Beef satay marinated overnight in chilli, garlic, coriander, galangal and palm sugar, then charcoal-grilled; sweeter and hotter than mainland satay.

places.name: Sate Rembiga Ibu Sinnaseh
places.note: The original stall in the Rembiga district that gave the satay its name.

places.name: Lesehan Taliwang Nada
places.note: Serves sate rembiga alongside the taliwang chicken menu.

food.name: Nasi balap puyung
food.desc: Rice packet from Puyung village: shredded chilli chicken, fried soy beans, dried squid and grated coconut, wrapped and eaten with the fingers.

places.name: Nasi Balap Puyung Inaq Esun
places.note: The famous Puyung recipe, with branches in the city as well as the home village.

places.name: Puyung village warungs
places.note: Original roadside stalls on the way to the airport; the benchmark version.

places.name: Pasar Cakranegara
places.note: Market vendors sell wrapped nasi balap for breakfast and lunch.

food.name: Sate bulayak
food.desc: Skewers of beef or offal served with a peanut-and-coconut sauce and bulayak, spiral rice cakes wrapped in palm leaf that you unwind as you eat.

places.name: Taman Narmada vendors
places.note: Sellers at the old royal water garden east of the city, the classic setting.

places.name: Suranadi forest park stalls
places.note: Cool hillside spot where satay and bulayak are sold to weekend visitors.

places.name: Warungs of Jalan Udayana
places.note: Evening food street in the city where satay grills set up after dark.

food.name: Beberuk terong and ares
food.desc: Beberuk is raw aubergine and long beans in lime-chilli sambal; ares is a Sasak stew of banana stem in coconut milk, served at ceremonies.

places.name: Rumah Makan Taliwang Irama
places.note: Beberuk terong comes as the cooling counterpart to the grilled chicken.

places.name: Pasar Cakranegara
places.note: Sasak home cooking including ares at the market food stalls.

places.name: Warungs of Kampung Karang Taliwang
places.note: Neighbourhood kitchens cooking the full Sasak spread, ares included.

food.name: Es kelapa muda
food.desc: Young coconut cracked open, the water poured over ice with the soft flesh scraped in and a little palm syrup. Mataram is Muslim, so drinks are alcohol-free.

places.name: Warungs at Loang Baloq beach
places.note: Beach stalls west of the city selling coconuts straight from the pile.

places.name: Pantai Ampenan

places.name: Warungs of Jalan Udayana

food.name: Kopi Lombok
food.desc: Robusta grown on the slopes of Rinjani, roasted dark and served as thick unfiltered kopi tubruk with plenty of sugar, or as sweet iced tea alongside.

landmarks: Islamic Center NTB (Hubbul Wathan Mosque)
Lombok's grandest landmark, a vast mosque whose 99-meter minaret and kaleidoscopic domes offer panoramic elevator views over Mataram.
Pura Meru
Lombok's largest Hindu temple, built in 1720 in Cakranegara, aligns three towering multi-tiered meru shrines to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma.
Mayura Water Palace
The 1744 Balinese royal garden of Cakranegara, where a floating pavilion sits serenely in a lotus-fringed ceremonial pool.
Taman Narmada
An 1805 royal park east of the city whose terraced pools replicate sacred Mount Rinjani and hold a fabled fountain of youth.
Pura Lingsar
Lombok's holiest temple compound, uniquely shared by Hindus and Wetu Telu Muslims, famed for its sacred eels and annual rice-cake battles.
West Nusa Tenggara State Museum (Museum Negeri NTB)
The province's chief museum unpacks Sasak, Balinese and Sumbawan cultures through krises, textiles and ceremonial treasures.
Ampenan Old Town
Mataram's faded Dutch-era port quarter, where pastel colonial shopfronts and a sunset-facing beach recall Lombok's cosmopolitan trading past.
Senggigi Beach
The island's original resort coast just north of Mataram, its sweeping bays serving postcard sunsets over the Lombok Strait toward Bali's Agung.
Banyumulek Pottery Village
A craft village minutes south of Mataram where generations of Sasak potters hand-coil and wood-fire Lombok's famous earthenware.
Sekarbela Pearl District
Mataram's pearl quarter, lined with workshops selling lustrous South Sea pearls harvested from Lombok's celebrated coastal farms.

train.note: There is no railway anywhere on Lombok or in Nusa Tenggara. Travel on the island is by road, and to reach it you take a ferry from Bali or fly into Lombok International Airport in the south.

bus.note: No international coaches. Mandalika terminal in Bertais handles island buses and the through services to Bali via the Lembar-Padangbai ferry, and on to Sumbawa via Kayangan - these are sold as single tickets including the crossing. Perama Tour (https://www.peramatour.com/) runs the tourist shuttle network between Mataram, Senggigi, the Gilis and Bali. Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/) for the local operators.

intl.to: Padangbai, Bali (Indonesia) - car ferry from Lembar, ~4-5 hr
Gili Trawangan, Gili Air & Gili Meno (Indonesia) - from Bangsal, ~30 min
intl.op: public boats and fast-boat operators — tickets at Bangsal harbour

intl.to: Poto Tano, Sumbawa (Indonesia) - from Kayangan, ~2 hr

ferry.note: No international sailings, but ferries are the backbone of travel here. The Lembar-Padangbai crossing to Bali runs around the clock and carries vehicles, taking four to five hours; fast boats from Senggigi and Bangsal do the same trip in under two but cost far more and are cancelled in rough seas. Bangsal is the gateway to the Gili islands, with cheap public boats leaving when full and pricier scheduled fast boats alongside.

half.name: Gili Nanggu and Gili Sudak
half.blurb: A cluster of small, quieter islands off Lombok's southwest coast with clear water for snorkeling, less crowded than the main Gilis.

full.name: Gili Islands (Trawangan, Meno, Air)
full.blurb: A trio of coral islands off Lombok's northwest coast reached by boat from Bangsal port, popular for snorkeling with sea turtles.

full.name: Pink Beach
full.blurb: A pale pink-sand beach on Lombok's southeastern coast, colored by crushed red coral mixed into the white sand.
